chapter: Return to Basie and leaving in 1948
title: Recording "The King" in 1946 and the band's postwar personnel
summary: Jones tells how he showed the band a groove on a sock cymbal for "The King," with Emmett Berry's solo and J. J. Johnson's last date.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Which he says, his is mine. I didn't know it was mine till after, because they had been recording for about 3 hours and I walked in with a sock cymbal and I said, 'Shadow, get up for a minute. Let me have this band for a minute. Fellows, it goes like this.' That's the last recording that J. J. Johnson made with the band.
J. J. Johnson was with Basie?
That's right, that's right. Emmett Berry played that terrific solo.
You hadn't mentioned that Emmett Berry was in the band even; I'm glad you mentioned that. What year was this in?
So he'd gotten Emmett Berry in there on trumpet now?
He had Emmett Berry; he had Sweets, Ed Lewis, because you remember Al Killian had left us earlier. Before I went in the Army he left us to join Charlie Barnet.
This was '47, you say? What year was this?
